intended_use: Requirement-to-oracle authoring aid for six public Rust candidate themes. This document is not a task registry, task manifest, run receipt, executable oracle, or admission record.

oracle_semantics.accepted_candidate: The candidate implementation satisfies every cited normative requirement for that case.
oracle_semantics.rejected_candidate: The candidate implementation violates at least one cited normative requirement.
oracle_semantics.unresolved_not_scored: The expected behavior cannot be adjudicated from the current frozen specification or required observation is unavailable; this is not automatically a candidate failure.
rules: Every oracle case cites one or more normative requirement IDs.
A valid alternative implementation must be accepted even when its source representation differs from the reference implementation.
A negative case must violate an explicit requirement; hidden tests may instantiate a disclosed requirement but may not add one.
Reference-patch acceptance and empty-patch rejection are eventual admission controls owned by the canonical task-admission contract, not results asserted by this document.
False accepts and false rejects must be reported separately when a qualified oracle and execution environment eventually exist.
Public development material is permanently ineligible for sealed-holdout status.

candidates.title: Cross-crate API and trait migration
candidates.mapping_rationale: The decisive failure is a public API change that breaks downstream crate consumers or compatibility paths across a workspace boundary.

requirements.statement: Malformed input is represented by a typed error result; the implementation does not panic or fabricate a success value.
The documented compatibility adapter remains callable and preserves its specified behavior.
Every in-scope consumer uses the normative API contract; no stale signature remains.
Callers can distinguish every error class that the specification declares observable.
Valid legacy inputs preserve the specified semantic result.
Deleting a public item, consumer, feature, test, or documented behavior is not an acceptable substitute for migration.

oracle_cases.scenario: A wrapper-based compatibility adapter delegates to the new API and preserves all specified legacy input/output semantics.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The requirements specify observable compatibility behavior, not one required implementation shape.

oracle_cases.scenario: A parser-internal error type is translated into a stable public error type while retaining every required error distinction.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The contract requires typed observable error classes but does not require one shared enum definition.

oracle_cases.scenario: The producer crate changes its public signature but one in-scope downstream crate still calls the stale signature.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: API-03 explicitly requires all in-scope consumers to use the normative contract.

oracle_cases.scenario: All parse failures become None or a generic string, erasing error distinctions required by the specification.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The implementation violates the typed failure and observable error-class requirements.

oracle_cases.scenario: The patch deletes the compatibility adapter or its documented consumer so the new API compiles.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: Deleting required compatibility surface is explicitly prohibited.

oracle_cases.scenario: A valid legacy request succeeds through the compatibility adapter after migration, while a malformed request produces the correct typed error through both entry points.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The composition case exercises compatibility and typed errors together, both explicitly required.

candidates.unresolved_before_fixture: Freeze exact public items, supported feature combinations, compatibility window, Rust toolchain and the set of error distinctions observable to downstream callers.

candidates.title: Async trait/API bounds and object-safe adapter
candidates.mapping_rationale: The decisive correctness surface is Rust type-system behavior: object safety, trait bounds, future sendability, associated types and borrowed lifetimes.

requirements.statement: The public async service contract is callable through the trait-object form required by the specification.
The returned future satisfies the declared Send bound across the target executor boundary.
The future may borrow the service instance for its declared lifetime; no undocumented 'static bound is imposed.
Success and error types preserve all required associated-type and error semantics.
All in-scope generic and trait-object consumers use the same normative contract.
Boxing, pinning, or macro expansion may change representation but not specified result, error, or cancellation behavior.

oracle_cases.scenario: An explicit object-safe method returns a pinned boxed Send future whose lifetime is tied to the borrowed service instance.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: This is one representation satisfying the stated type and behavior contract.

oracle_cases.scenario: An approved async-trait transformation provides the same object-safe, Send, borrowed-lifetime and error behavior.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The specification fixes the observable contract, not a particular macro or source spelling.

oracle_cases.scenario: A future captures a non-Send value and cannot cross the required executor boundary.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The candidate violates the explicit Send requirement.

oracle_cases.scenario: The implementation adds an unnecessary 'static bound and rejects valid borrowed service implementations.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The requirement permits a future to borrow the service for its declared lifetime.

oracle_cases.scenario: Generic consumers compile but the required trait-object consumer cannot invoke the service.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The public trait-object call path is explicitly required.

oracle_cases.scenario: A borrowed service is called through the required trait-object path on a Send executor; the future is Send, preserves typed errors and ends the borrow at the correct lifetime.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: This composes object safety, Send, lifetime and error requirements.

candidates.unresolved_before_fixture: Freeze the public trait signature, executor, macro dependency policy, MSRV, target triples, object-safety form and permitted lifetime relationships.

candidates.title: Deterministic reproduction of an event-processing defect
candidates.mapping_rationale: The task is centered on reproducing a bounded stateful failure, isolating its root cause and demonstrating that the repair removes the reproduced defect without collateral regression.

requirements.statement: The supplied baseline defect is triggered by a deterministic, disclosed event/failure schedule rather than timing luck.
The reproduction identifies the triggering preconditions and the observable incorrect state transition.
The repair addresses the causal defect, not merely the displayed symptom or one fixed input trace.
The repair preserves required behavior across the disclosed retry, replay and restart conditions.
The repair preserves unrelated protected invariants and does not suppress errors or hide failed work.
A failure to observe the required state because of unavailable instrumentation or infrastructure is unresolved, not a successful repair.

oracle_cases.scenario: The declared baseline schedule reproducibly triggers the documented duplicate-effect or lost-acknowledgement defect.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The known baseline reproducer is required for task validity; this is not a candidate solution result.

oracle_cases.scenario: A transactional inbox/outbox or an equivalent atomic deduplication design removes the defect and preserves the declared invariants.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The requirements constrain observable durability and replay behavior, not a specific storage design.

oracle_cases.scenario: The repair adds a sleep or retry delay that makes the supplied trace pass without fixing the underlying race or state inconsistency.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: A timing workaround does not address the causal defect.

oracle_cases.scenario: The repair handles sequential duplicate delivery but fails when the same event is replayed after a restart.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: Restart replay is an explicitly stated condition.

oracle_cases.scenario: The repair makes the reproducer disappear by acknowledging all events as successful while silently dropping failed work.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The declared terminal outcome and protected-work invariants must remain truthful.

oracle_cases.scenario: The runner cannot expose the required durable state or crash boundary, so the oracle cannot determine whether the event was committed before acknowledgement.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The requirement explicitly distinguishes missing observability from a candidate failure.

candidates.unresolved_before_fixture: Freeze the event schedule, durable-effect definition, acknowledgement boundary, storage assumptions, deterministic crash/restart instrumentation and protected invariants.

candidates.title: Workspace command and path boundary
candidates.mapping_rationale: The task's primary acceptance construct is preventing untrusted workspace content from crossing command-execution or filesystem-authority boundaries.

requirements.statement: Untrusted path and project content is never interpolated into a shell command string.
Executable selection and arguments are passed as separate values to the process API.
Filesystem operations remain confined to the declared workspace root.
Absolute paths, parent traversal and disallowed symlink escapes are rejected under the stated filesystem threat model.
Invalid paths and process failures produce explicit non-success outcomes rather than silent success.
The implementation does not broaden command or filesystem permissions to bypass an acceptance check.

oracle_cases.scenario: A valid in-root path containing spaces and shell metacharacters is passed as a single data argument through direct argv.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The requirements prohibit shell interpretation, not legitimate data characters.

oracle_cases.scenario: A descriptor-relative or platform-specific safe-open implementation enforces the declared root boundary.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The requirement specifies containment behavior, not a required path API.

oracle_cases.scenario: Untrusted path content is concatenated into sh -c or another shell command string.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: This directly violates the no-shell-interpolation rule.

oracle_cases.scenario: A sibling-prefix path or symlink escape is accepted as inside the workspace.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The path is outside the declared authority boundary.

oracle_cases.scenario: All process errors are caught and converted to success, or an unrestricted shell is enabled to make the check pass.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The behavior hides failures or expands authority beyond the contract.

oracle_cases.scenario: A legitimate in-root path containing metacharacters is handled as data, while a symlink resolving outside the root is rejected.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: This tests command/data separation and path authority together.

candidates.unresolved_before_fixture: Pin OS and filesystem behavior, allowed executable policy, symlink race threat model, normalization rules and whether descriptor-relative operations are required.

candidates.title: Cargo feature and target composition
candidates.mapping_rationale: The task is defined by the correctness of an explicitly declared matrix of Cargo feature combinations, target-specific dependencies and environment assumptions.

requirements.statement: Every supported feature combination is explicitly listed in the frozen task specification.
Each supported no-default-features configuration builds without importing default-only APIs.
Platform-specific dependencies and modules are gated for the declared supported targets.
Mutually exclusive features fail clearly or select the documented behavior; they do not silently choose an unintended backend.
Supported feature combinations preserve the required public protocol/API behavior.
The build does not rely on undeclared host packages, ambient environment variables or locally cached artifacts.

oracle_cases.scenario: An explicit backend-selection module and target-specific dependency declarations satisfy every declared feature/target combination.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The contract specifies the supported matrix and behavior, not one Cargo.toml layout.

oracle_cases.scenario: A supported no-default build uses a small adapter boundary and preserves the required public API without enabling defaults.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The behavior and feature surface remain intact while implementation structure may vary.

oracle_cases.scenario: Only the default feature set builds; a declared supported no-default configuration references an unavailable symbol.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The no-default configuration is explicitly in the supported matrix.

oracle_cases.scenario: An unconditional module import requires a platform-specific dependency on a target where that dependency is unavailable.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The declared target support requires correct platform gating.

oracle_cases.scenario: Mutually exclusive backends both compile but the implementation silently selects an undocumented backend.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The behavior contradicts the explicitly specified conflict policy.

oracle_cases.scenario: A supported no-default feature build on a non-primary target uses no undeclared host dependency and preserves the required protocol behavior.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The declared matrix requires this simultaneous feature, target and environment combination.

candidates.unresolved_before_fixture: Freeze Rust toolchain, exact feature matrix, supported targets, optional dependency versions, cross-compilation environment and clean-build assumptions.

candidates.title: Exact streaming top-k under bounded resources
candidates.mapping_rationale: The task requires exact semantics and a measured resource improvement under a frozen workload; speed cannot compensate for an incorrect result or manipulated measurement.

requirements.statement: Results equal the exact top-k under the declared total ordering after every accepted update.
Equal scores use the specified deterministic tie-breaker.
Insert, update and remove operations update the ranking exactly once and do not retain stale entries.
k=0, empty input, fewer than k elements and duplicate keys have explicit specified results.
NaN, infinities and signed zero follow the declared numeric-domain policy.
Time and memory satisfy the explicitly declared workload and resource bound.
Caching is allowed only when contract-permitted and semantically correct for unseen in-scope inputs, invalidation, cold starts and resource limits.

oracle_cases.scenario: An indexed binary heap plus key-index map produces exact results and deterministic ties after all declared operations.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The implementation strategy is an alternative to the reference data structure and satisfies the stated semantics.

oracle_cases.scenario: An ordered tree structure plus key index produces the same exact top-k behavior.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The benchmark contract is semantic, not tied to heap internals.

oracle_cases.scenario: A lazy heap keeps stale entries after updates/removals and returns an obsolete top-k member.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The current result must match the exact state after each operation.

oracle_cases.scenario: Tie ordering is nondeterministic or a boundary case such as k=0 is handled contrary to the declared numeric and boundary policy.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The candidate violates explicit tie/boundary semantics.

oracle_cases.scenario: A fixed visible workload is memoized, but unseen in-scope values or invalidation cause incorrect results; reported speedup uses only the cached path.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The behavior violates generalization and measurement integrity even if the visible input appears fast.

oracle_cases.scenario: An item at the k-boundary is updated, another item is removed and two remaining items tie; the result reflects all operations and the deterministic tie-breaker.
oracle_cases.why_spec_derived: The interaction combines the required update, removal and tie semantics.

candidates.unresolved_before_fixture: Freeze key type, total ordering, numeric policy, tie-breaker, workload distribution, memory ceiling, hardware and measurement protocol.
